claims.text: The India Meteorological Department's Bhubaneswar Met Centre reported that a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal persisted at 8:30 a.m. on October 23, 2026.
The IMD predicted moderate to heavy rainfall across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry until October 26.
A TNSTC bus driver was killed and the conductor was seriously injured when a mudslide and uprooted trees buried a bus near Burliar in the Nilgiris district on October 24.
Last year's cyclone Montha was classified as a severe cyclonic storm.
The Odisha government announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts on October 28 and 29 to ensure zero casualties.
Persistent heavy rains flooded the Sri Lankan Tamil refugee camp in Puliyampatti, inundating more than 100 houses.
District Collector S. Durga Moorthy visited the flooded Sri Lankan Tamil refugee camp in Puliyampatti to assess the damage.
Telangana is experiencing a rainfall deficit and drinking water shortages due to the influence of El Nino.
Heavy overnight rainfall triggered landslides at more than 10 locations along the Coonoor-Mettupalayam National Highway.
Government bus driver Janakaraj died and conductor Kesavan was injured when a landslide struck near Barliyar on the Mettupalayam-Ooty road.
A goods vehicle transporting chickens was swept into a gorge during a landslide in Barliyar, though the driver escaped unhurt.
Heavy rainfall in Barliyar village completely washed away a house, though its occupants escaped unharmed.
Stranded bus passengers in the Nilgiris district were evacuated and relocated to relief camps in Coonoor.
Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru advised the public to avoid traveling on affected roads unless for emergency purposes.
The Nilgiris district administration set up emergency helpline 1077 for residents seeking assistance during the heavy rains.
The Northeast monsoon has set in over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, and Mahe.
The IMD warned that a low-pressure area over the south Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26.
Coastal and western districts of West Bengal are expected to receive heavy rainfall starting October 28.
The IMD advised fisherfolk not to venture into the sea from October 26 onwards.
Thunderstorms with wind gusts reaching up to 40 km per hour are expected over all south Bengal districts starting October 28.
A very severe cyclonic storm carries maximum sustained wind speeds between 118 km/h and 221 km/h.
During cyclone Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam reached 65 km/h.
On Saturday evening, the depression in the Bay of Bengal lay centered about 510 km off the Andaman Islands and 820 km off the Visakhapatnam coast.
The IMD issued a red alert for 13 districts in Andhra Pradesh for October 27 and 28.
The cyclonic storm is projected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the noon of October 28.
Simhadripuram in YSR Kadapa district received 81.5 mm of rainfall between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on Saturday.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to remain alert and develop a comprehensive flood management and water conservation plan.
The Regional Meteorological Centre issued a red alert for isolated places in Theni, Dindigul, and Madurai districts for extremely heavy rainfall.
Out of 620 online weather stations in Tamil Nadu, 493 recorded rainfall by 8:30 a.m. on Saturday.
The Burliyar weather station recorded 25 cm of rainfall in the 24-hour period ending 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, the highest in Tamil Nadu.
A persistent low-pressure area over the Southeast Arabian Sea and adjoining Lakshadweep area influenced rainfall along the Western Ghats.
